name: MD-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Glenn Ivey running with a large cash advantage
model.rationale: A D+39 Maryland seat with an incumbent Democrat who has raised over $670,000 against an unknown, unfunded Republican leaves essentially no path for an upset, and prediction markets agree at 97% for the Democrat.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or an unexpectedly strong third-party Green showing could narrow the margin, though not the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Glenn Ivey, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Maryland district that leans Democratic by 39 points. He enters the general election with about $459,000 on hand after raising more than $670,000, while Republican George McDermott has reported no fundraising and little public profile. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no meaningful financial support.

Prediction markets put Ivey's chances at roughly 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, incumbency, and the large financial imbalance, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic win.
